newsitem.title: HONG KONG: British commander in HK agrees China advance force.
newsitem.headline: British commander in HK agrees China advance force.

text.p: The commander of the British garrison in Hong Kong said on Sunday it was necessary for Beijing to send a group of advance troops to the territory before it reverts to China next year.

"It's necessary for the People's Liberation Army to have a small element here beforehand to do the necessary administrative preparation before the PLA themselves come in on July 1," Major-General Bryan Dutton told reporters after attending a public function.
Britain is handing Hong Kong back to China at midnight next June 30, when the PLA troops will replace the British garrison.
Chinese and British negotiators held talks last week over the advance party but failed to reach an agreement.
The two countries' diplomats only agreed that if the Chinese troops were to arrive before the handover, they would abide by the colony's laws.
Britain is seeking details on the size of the PLA vanguard and their functions before making a decision.

The arrival of the PLA is viewed with some trepidation in Hong Kong where the images of troops cracking down on the student-led pro-democracy movement in June 1989 remains branded in the collective memory.
China has said the size of the future garrison will not exceed that of the British garrison during its peak when it numbered about 10,000 troops.
